children: Iron ore futures fell for a fifth straight session on Tuesday, weighed down by rising shipments, while elevated coke prices squeezed steel mill margins and clouded the demand outlook.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
was 0.49% lower at 708 yuan ($105.52) a metric ton, as of 0255 GMT.
The benchmark October iron ore (SZZFV6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.15% lower at $96.45 a ton.
Global iron ore shipments rose 1.59 million tons week-on-week to 35.17 million tons in the week to September 13, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.
Coke prices remain high, with some mills entering maintenance amid tight supply, weakening rigid demand for iron ore, analysts from Shanghai Metals Market said in a note.
With demand contracting and supply holding steady, ore prices are likely to stay weak in the near term, the analysts said.
China's daily crude steel output in August fell 3% from the month before to hit an eight-month low, as some steelmakers scaled down operations amid plunging margins.
China's new home prices also extended declines in August, official data showed, underscoring the persistent drag from the country's prolonged property downturn.

Steel mills may have some appetite to restock iron ore ahead of holidays at the end of the month, though the sharp drop in profit margins is likely to keep that restocking drive limited, analysts from broker Chaos Ternary Futures said in a note.
